interface.signature: dict: List[str], N: int, K: int -> str

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(word, str) and len(word) > 0 for word in dict)
preconditions.description: Every element in `dict` is a non-empty string.
The integer `N` matches the length of the input list `dict`.
The integer `K` is between 1 and 26 (inclusive), representing the number of unique starting alphabets.
Every word in `dict` has a length of at most 50 characters.

preconditions.expression: all(word[0] in set(dict[0]) for word in dict)
preconditions.description: All words in `dict` start with a character present in the first word of `dict` (implied by the problem's context of 'starting alphabets').

preconditions.expression: all(word1 <= word2 for i in range(N - 1) for word1, word2 in [(dict[i], dict[i + 1])])
preconditions.description: The input `dict` is sorted lexicographically according to the alien language's character order.

postconditions.description: The returned string has exactly `K` unique characters, representing the order of the alien language's alphabet.

postconditions.expression: all(c in return_value for word in dict for c in word)
postconditions.description: Every character in every word of `dict` appears in the returned string.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value.index(c1) < return_value.index(c2) for i in range(N - 1) for c1, c2 in [(dict[i][j], dict[i + 1][j]) if dict[i][j] != dict[i + 1][j] else (None, None) for j in range(min(len(dict[i]), len(dict[i + 1]))) if c1 is not None and c2 is not None])
postconditions.description: For every pair of adjacent words in `dict`, the first differing character in the pair must appear earlier in `return_value` than the second differing character, preserving the sorted order of the alien language.
